question: Should OpenClaw adopt capability-gated native append as a permanent built-in write-tool and public Plugin SDK bridge contract?
rationale: The code can be evaluated technically, but only an owner can accept the long-term model-facing API, backend capability rules, plugin obligations, and retry semantics.

options.title: Close pending sponsorship
options.body: Close this technically strong proposal now and invite an owner to sponsor and reopen it when the permanent API direction is confirmed.

options.title: Sponsor the contract
options.body: Explicitly approve the built-in parameter and optional bridge method, then complete normal current-head review and CI before landing.

options.title: Request a narrower design
options.body: Keep core overwrite-only until maintainers define a smaller internal or non-public append boundary that does not commit the Plugin SDK.

recommendation.title: Close pending sponsorship
recommendation.body: Close this technically strong proposal now and invite an owner to sponsor and reopen it when the permanent API direction is confirmed.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history spans the sandbox filesystem security boundary, OpenShell behavior, and adjacent agent-tool architecture.
